entrance.name: National Forest Recreation Day Pass
entrance.waived_by: a Northwest Forest Pass or an Interagency Annual, Senior, Access or Military pass

fees_note: No camping fee: the National Forest Recreation Day Pass ($5 per vehicle, valid only on the date printed, so one night spans two passes) or a $30 annual Northwest Forest Pass, or an Interagency Annual/Senior/Access/Military pass. summary: Pass is the Northwest Forest Pass system ($5 day pass / $30 annual), interagency passes honored, Discover Pass not; modelled as entrance (vehicle_day, departure_day, annual 30) with all_in nightly 10.
flag: nightly raised 5 -> 10: the $5 day pass expires 11:59 PM on its date, so an overnight stay needs the arrival and departure days (departure_day: true), as Virginia's WMA access permit is modelled. If AWH reads one night as one $5 pass, set nightly 5 and drop departure_day. Used entrance rather than prereq_pass because only entrance holds departure_day and the $30 annual option.

prereq_pass.name: LTVA short-visit permit (Sep 15-Apr 15)
prereq_pass.waived_by: an LTVA long-term permit ($180, valid for the whole Sep 15-Apr 15 season)

fees_note: BLM LTVA, two fee seasons (BLM page read 2026-11-07). Sep 15-Apr 15: an LTVA permit is required, $40 short-visit permit for any 14 consecutive days (renewable without limit) or $180 long-term permit for the whole season or any part of it. Apr 16-Sep 14: $15 per vehicle per night or $75 a year per vehicle, up to 5 people per vehicle, $1 each person over 5 ($10 per vehicle for day use); maximum stay 14 days in a 28-day period. nightly_low is the Apr 16-Sep 14 night, nightly_high the cheapest in-season night (a $40 short-visit permit); the schema has no seasonal price, so the season rides in the permit names. A 2024 Yuma Field Office draft business plan proposed $600 long-term / $200 short-term (30 days); BLM's own pages still post $180/$40 as of 2026-11-07.
note: BLM Long-Term Visitor Area just S of Quartzsite on US-95, ~11,400 acres of open desert in 4 units (South/West/North/Tyson Wash). Vault toilets, water faucets, dump station with water, trash, ramada. Flat drive-in desert that fits any RV; public BLM permit camping, not a membership or residential park. --Claude
sources: https://www.blm.gov/visit/la-posa-long-term-visitor-area ('The LTVA long term permit ($180)' Sep 15-Apr 15; 'The LTVA short-visit permit ($40)' any 14 consecutive days, renewable; Apr 16-Sep 14 '$10 per vehicle for day-use', '$15 per vehicle for overnight use, or $75 annually per vehicle, for up to 5 people per vehicle', '$1 fee ... over the 5 person limit'; 'maximum stay is 14 days in a 28-day period', read 2026-11-07)
summary: LTVA fees confirmed on BLM's page ($40/14-day or $180/season permit Sep 15-Apr 15; $15/vehicle/night or $75/yr Apr 16-Sep 14); modelled as nightly 15-40 all_in with the season named in prereq_pass and entrance; permit sentence cut from the note.
flag: The schema has no seasonal price: nightly_low 15 is the summer night, nightly_high 40 the cheapest in-season night, and the two permit objects carry their seasons only in their names, so a chip reads both as if both applied. The cut note sentence's 'renewable' and the 14-days-in-28 summer stay limit now live only in fees.note (not shown in the popup). BLM's pages do not say whether interagency passes discount LTVA permits, so no waiver is recorded. A 2024 BLM Yuma draft plan proposed $600/$200; BLM still posts $180/$40.
